questions.question: Which of the following statements about eutrophication is correct?
questions.option_1: It happens when too less nitrogen is present in the water, causing reduced growth of plants and algae.
questions.option_2: It is a beneficial process for environment restoration.
questions.option_3: It happens when too much nitrogen enriches the water, causing excessive growth of plants and algae.
questions.option_4: It happens when too much carbon enriches the water, causing excessive growth of bacteria and reduced growth of plants.
questions.solution:
Eutrophication occurs when excessive nitrogen or phosphorus enriches a body of water, leading to the rapid growth of algae and aquatic plants.
  • This 'algal bloom' blocks sunlight and uses up dissolved oxygen as the plants die and decompose.
  • The resulting lack of oxygen leads to the death of fish and other aquatic life, creating dead zones.
  • Fact: Human activities, like agricultural runoff containing fertilizers, are the primary cause of accelerated eutrophication.

questions.question: Which group of animals has a segmented spinal column together with a few primitive forms in which the backbone is represented by a notochord?
questions.solution:
The subphylum Vertebrata (part of Phylum Chordata) is characterized by the presence of a notochord in the embryonic stage, which is replaced by a segmented spinal column (backbone) in adults.
  • Primitive forms like Hagfish still retain the notochord into adulthood.
  • Vertebrates also possess a well-defined head, a closed circulatory system, and a multi-chambered heart.

questions.question: The loss of water in the form of water droplets from leaves of plants is called _____.
questions.solution:
Guttation is the loss of water in the form of liquid droplets from the margins of leaves.
  • It occurs through specialized structures called hydathodes, usually at night or early morning when root pressure is high and transpiration is low.
  • Note: This is different from Transpiration, where water is lost as vapor through the stomata.

questions.question: In which of the following plants do roots arise from parts of a plant other than the radicle?
questions.solution:
In Monstera, the roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle; these are known as Adventitious roots.
  • The Radicle is the part of the embryo that normally develops into the primary root (Taproot).
  • Other examples of adventitious roots include the prop roots of a Banyan tree and the stilt roots of Maize.

questions.question: How do the muscle cells help in movement?
questions.option_1: The blood flow of the cells helps in movement.
questions.option_2: The thickness of the cell layer helps in movement.
questions.option_3: The lining of the vessels inside help in movement.
questions.option_4: The contraction and relaxation of these cells result in movement.
questions.solution:
Muscle cells facilitate movement through their unique ability for contraction and relaxation.
  • They contain specialized proteins called Actin and Myosin that slide past each other to shorten the cell.
  • This mechanical work generates the force needed to move limbs, circulate blood, or push food through the digestive tract.

questions.question: Which of the following enzymes are essential of DNA replication in an animal cell?
questions.option_3: Topoisomerase, DNA ligase, DNA polymerase, DNA primase
questions.option_4: Reverse transcriptase, DNA polymerase, DNA primase
questions.solution:
DNA replication in animal cells requires a specific set of enzymes working in a coordinated fashion:
  • Helicase: Unwinds the DNA double helix.
  • Topoisomerase: Relieves the tension caused by unwinding.
  • DNA Primase: Synthesizes a short RNA primer to start the process.
  • DNA Polymerase: Adds new nucleotides to the growing DNA strand.
  • DNA Ligase: Seals gaps between DNA fragments (Okazaki fragments).

questions.question: What do you mean by semiconservative DNA replication?
questions.option_1: RNA is dependent on DNA for the synthesis of proteins
questions.option_2: After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have one parental and one newly synthesised strand.
questions.option_3: After the completion of replication, each DNA molecule would have two parental and two newly synthesised strand.
questions.option_4: DNA is dependent on RNA for the synthesis of proteins
questions.solution:
Semiconservative replication means that after DNA is copied, each new DNA molecule consists of one original parental strand and one newly synthesized strand.
  • This mechanism ensures that the genetic information is accurately preserved and passed on to daughter cells.
  • This was famously proven by the Meselson-Stahl experiment.

questions.question: Which of the following causes enlargement and extension growth of cells?
questions.solution:
Turgor pressure is the internal pressure exerted by the fluid inside a plant cell against the cell wall, which causes cell enlargement and extension growth.
  • When a cell takes in water via osmosis, the vacuole expands, pushing against the wall and stretching it.
  • This pressure is vital for maintaining the structural rigidity of non-woody plants.

questions.question: Why is the six membered cyclic structure of glucose called a pyranose structure?
questions.option_1: Furan is a five membered cyclic compound, with one oxygen and four carbon atoms.
questions.option_2: Pyran is a non-cyclic organic compound, with one oxygen atom and five carbon atoms in the ring.
questions.option_3: Furan is a five membered non-cyclic compound, with one oxygen and four carbon atoms.
questions.option_4: Pyran is a cyclic organic compound, with one oxygen atom and five carbon atoms in the ring.
questions.solution:
Glucose is called a pyranose because its six-membered cyclic structure resembles a heterocyclic organic compound called Pyran.
  • A pyran ring consists of five carbon atoms and one oxygen atom.
  • Note: Fructose often forms a five-membered furanose ring, resembling Furan (four carbons and one oxygen).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a mutation-based disease?
questions.solution:
Malaria is not a mutation-based disease; it is an infectious disease caused by the Plasmodium parasite and transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes.
  • Down syndrome, Sickle cell anaemia, and Phenylketonuria are all genetic disorders resulting from chromosomal abnormalities or specific gene mutations.

questions.question: The cell wall of bacteria is made up of:
questions.solution:
The cell wall of Bacteria is primarily composed of Peptidoglycan (also known as murein).
  • It is a polymer of sugars and amino acids that provides structural strength and protects the cell from osmotic pressure.
  • Comparison: Plant cell walls are made of Cellulose, and fungal cell walls are made of Chitin.

questions.question: Identify a carbohydrate but does not fit into the definition.
questions.solution:
Rhamnose is a carbohydrate that does not fit the traditional general formula for carbohydrates, which is $C_n(H_2O)_n$.
  • The chemical formula for Rhamnose is $C_6H_{12}O_5$.
  • While it is a sugar (a deoxy-hexose), it lacks the exact ratio of hydrogen to oxygen found in 'hydrates of carbon.'

questions.question: Which of the following muscles regulates the exit of food from the stomach into the small intestine?
questions.solution:
The Pyloric Sphincter is the ring of muscle that regulates the passage of partially digested food (chyme) from the stomach into the small intestine.
  • It acts as a valve, opening to allow small amounts of food through and closing to prevent backflow.

questions.question: Mendel proposed the law of independent assortment on the basis of __________.
questions.solution:
Gregor Mendel proposed the Law of Independent Assortment based on his results from Dihybrid crosses (crosses involving two pairs of contrasting traits).
  • The law states that the alleles for different traits segregate independently of one another during gamete formation.

questions.question: In which year did Wilhelm Johannsen coin the term ‘gene’ to describe the Mendelian units of heredity?
questions.solution:
In 1909, the Danish botanist Wilhelm Johannsen coined the term 'Gene' to describe the fundamental units of heredity that Mendel had called 'factors.'
  • He also introduced the terms Genotype and Phenotype during the same period.

questions.question: The phenomenon of the interaction between nonallelic genes at two or more loci resulting in one gene masking the phenotypic expression of another gene, is known as:
questions.solution:
Epistasis is a genetic interaction where the expression of one gene masks or interferes with the phenotypic expression of another gene at a different locus.
  • This is a form of non-allelic interaction.
  • An example is the coat color in Labrador retrievers, where one gene determines the pigment color and another determines if that pigment is actually deposited in the fur.

questions.question: In which year did a trio of scientists, Avery, MacLeod and McCarty, prove that except viruses, all living organisms have DNA as their genetic material?
questions.solution:
In 1944, Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty published their research proving that DNA is the substance responsible for heredity.
  • They expanded on Frederick Griffith's earlier experiments to show that DNA (not protein) was the 'transforming principle.'

questions.question: Which of the following is a rare group of genetic disorders caused by mutations of certain genes affecting the colour (pigmentation) of the skin, hair and eyes?
questions.solution:
Albinism is a group of rare genetic disorders characterized by a lack of melanin pigment in the skin, hair, and eyes.
  • It is caused by mutations in genes that provide instructions for producing or distributing melanin.
  • People with albinism are highly sensitive to UV radiation and often have vision problems.

questions.question: Which of the following statements most accurately describes the Cyclostomata group?
questions.option_1: They are characterised by having an elongated eel-like body, circular mouth, slimy skin and are scaleless.
questions.option_2: They are ectothermic animals having mucus glands in the skin, and a three-chambered heart.
questions.option_3: They are warm-blooded, oviparous, bipedal, feathered, winged and toothless vertebrates.
questions.option_4: Their skin is covered with scales/plates and their hearts have only two chambers.
questions.solution:
Cyclostomata (jawless fishes) are characterized by an elongated, eel-like body, a circular sucking mouth without jaws, and a lack of scales and paired fins.
  • They have a cartilaginous skeleton and are mostly ectoparasites on other fish (e.g., Petromyzon or Lamprey).

questions.question: Which of the following animals can change their gender during their life span?
questions.solution:
Certain Snails (and some fish like clownfish) are capable of sequential hermaphroditism, meaning they can change their gender during their life span.
  • This adaptation is often triggered by environmental factors or social hierarchy within a population.

questions.question: In a dihybrid cross between two heterozygous fruit flies with brown bodies and red eyes (BbEe X BbEe), what will be the probability of getting BBEE genotype?
questions.solution:
In a dihybrid cross of BbEe X BbEe, the probability of obtaining the BBEE genotype is $1/16$.
  • According to the Punnett square for a dihybrid cross, there are 16 total possible combinations.
  • Only 1 out of those 16 combinations will be homozygous dominant for both traits ($1/4$ for BB $ imes 1/4$ for EE).

questions.question: What is the main sense organ that virtual reality displays are aiming for?
questions.solution:
The primary sense organ targeted by Virtual Reality (VR) displays is Vision.
  • VR headsets use stereoscopic displays to create a 3D environment, tricking the brain into perceiving depth and immersion through the eyes.

questions.question: Which of the following sequences is correct, according to taxonomy?
questions.solution:
The correct taxonomic hierarchy from most broad to most specific is: Phylum $ ightarrow$ Class $ ightarrow$ Order $ ightarrow$ Family $ ightarrow$ Genus $ ightarrow$ Species.
  • Mnemonic: Keep Pots Clean Or Family Gets Sick (Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species).

questions.question: Identify the INCORRECT statement regarding invertebrates from the options given below.
questions.option_1: They possess a backbone and an internal skeleton.
questions.option_2: They have radial or bilateral body symmetry.
questions.option_3: They have a pair of solid nerve cords, situated ventrally and bearing segmentally arranged ganglia.
questions.option_4: They have open circulatory system as there is no organisation in the distribution.
questions.solution:
The statement that Invertebrates 'possess a backbone' is incorrect.
  • By definition, invertebrates are animals that lack a vertebral column (backbone).
  • They make up about 95% of all animal species on Earth.

questions.question: Who was the first person to conduct a systematic study of chromosomes during division and called this process mitosis?
questions.solution:
Walther Flemming was the first to systematically study chromosomes during cell division and is credited with naming the process Mitosis.
  • He used salamander larvae to observe the 'thread-like' behavior of chromatin during division.

questions.question: In the context of DNA, which of the following principles governs the process of transcription?
questions.solution:
The process of Transcription (copying DNA into RNA) is governed by the Principle of Complementarity.
  • Adenine pairs with Uracil (in RNA), and Guanine pairs with Cytosine.
  • This ensures that the genetic code from the DNA template is accurately transcribed into the messenger RNA (mRNA).

questions.question: Which of the following is a part of apical meristem found in roots.
questions.solution:
The Protoderm is a primary meristem found in the root apical meristem.
  • It is the outermost layer of the apical meristem and eventually differentiates into the Epidermis (rhizodermis) of the root.

questions.question: In a symport:
questions.option_1: a molecule moves across a membrane dependent of other molecules
questions.option_2: both molecules cross the membrane in the same direction
questions.option_3: a molecule moves across a membrane independent of other molecules
questions.option_4: both molecules cross the membrane in the opposite direction
questions.solution:
In a Symport (a type of cotransport), two different molecules cross the membrane in the same direction at the same time.
  • Note: In an Antiport, molecules move in opposite directions, and in a Uniport, a single molecule moves independently.

questions.question: Which of the Mendel's laws states that a diploid organism passes a randomly selected allele for a trait to its offspring, such that the offspring inherit one allele from each parent?
questions.solution:
Mendel's Law of Segregation states that during the formation of gametes, the two alleles for a trait separate so that each gamete receives only one allele.
  • This restores the diploid state when two gametes fuse during fertilization.

questions.question: Which of the following is a medium-sized globular protein that acts as a pancreatic serine protease found in the digestive system of many vertebrates?
questions.solution:
Trypsin is a serine protease produced in the pancreas as an inactive precursor called trypsinogen.
  • It is secreted into the small intestine where it breaks down proteins into smaller peptides.

questions.question: In honey bees, _____
questions.option_1: males are diploid and females are haploid.
questions.option_2: males are triploid and females are tetraploid.
questions.option_3: males are haploid and females are diploid.
questions.option_4: males are tetraploid and females are triploid.
questions.solution:
In a honey bee colony, males are haploid and females (Queens and Workers) are diploid.
  • This is known as the Haplodiploid sex-determination system.
  • Males (drones) develop from unfertilized eggs via parthenogenesis, while females develop from fertilized eggs.

questions.question: Which of the following is a food-borne disease caused by the consumption of contaminated food or beverages?
questions.solution:
Cholera is a severe food-borne and water-borne disease caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae.
  • It is typically spread through the consumption of contaminated water or food and causes acute watery diarrhea and dehydration.
